name: Eiichi Kuriwada
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2024)
forbes_bio: Eiichi Kuriwada's father, Kiyoshi Sagawa, founded a package delivery firm in 1957; now called Sagawa Express, it's Japan's No. 2 delivery outfit.
Sagawa Express parent SG Holdings listed its shares on the Tokyo Stock Exchange in December 2017.
Kuriwada is chairman and CEO of SG Holdings.
Shares of the company had soared on the back of a jump in online buying during the pandemic  but have since declined.
forbes_facts: In the early 1990s, Sagawa Express was the focus of a scandal; an executive was convicted of paying off politicians.
Sagawa, a billionaire in 1992, resigned that year; neither he nor Kuriwada were charged as part of the scandal.

name: Laurent Junique
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2023); Hurun Global (2023-2026)
forbes_bio: Laurent Junique is the CEO and founder of Singapore-based call center and business process outsourcing firm TDCX.
TDCX went public on the New York Stock Exchange in 2021. In 2024, Junique took the company private in a deal valuing it at around $1 billion.
Junique, a French citizen, founded TDCX as a 29-year-old in 1995 after a two-year stint at consumer goods giant Unilever.
TDCX counts Meta and Airbnb among its key clients.

name: Zhu Xingliang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2011-2023); Hurun Global (2014-2023); Hurun China (2007-2026)
forbes_bio: Zhu Xingliang is the largest shareholder of Suzhou Gold Mantis Construction Decoration, a pioneer in China's interior design and decoration industry.
Zhu founded Suzhou Gold Mantis in 1993.
Gold Mantis has done interior/exterior decorating, landscaping, design and other work for some of China's eminent new structures.

name: Brian Lawson
forbes_bio: Brian Lawson is a vice chair of Brookfield, a Toronto-based alternative investment firm with $1 trillion in assets under management.
Lawson joined Brookfield in 1988, when it was called Brascan, and served as the firm's CFO from 2002 to 2020.
Lawson began his career as an accountant at Touche Ross, a predecessor to Deloitte.
His family's foundation supports nutrition research and established the University of Toronto's Joannah & Brian Lawson Centre for Child Nutrition.

name: Xia Zhisheng
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2021); Hurun Global (2021); Hurun China (2015-2021)
forbes_bio: Xia Zhisheng is the vice chairman Zhejiang Meida Industrial, a supplier of integrated stoves.
Xia started his own business in 1979 with 5000 yuan in Zhejiang Province-an electroplating operation-and manufacturing electronic items in 1980s.
Xia founded the predecessor of Meida in 1995.
Xia's daughter Xia Lan chairs Meida.

name: Marcelo Kalim
forbes_bio: Marcelo Kalim cofounded digital bank C6 in 2018; it sold a 40% stake to JP Morgan in June 2021 for an undisclosed amount.
C6 says that as of 2021 it had attracted 7 million customers since it launched in 2019.
Prior to C6, Kalim was a significant shareholder and longtime executive of Brazil's BTG Pactual, Latin America's largest investment bank.

name: Jean Burelle
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2020); Forbes annual (2014-2016); Hurun Global (2017-2020); Wikidata (2021)

name: Madan Mohanka
forbes_bio: Madan Mohanka is the chairman of Kolkata-based Tega Industries, which manufactures products such as mill liners and conveyor components that are used for mining, mineral processing and material handling.
Mohanka, a trained engineer, founded the company in 1976 in collaboration with a Swedish firm, initially targeting the mining industry.
Today, Tega Industries has more than 700 customers across 70 countries and operations in Chile, South Africa and Australia.
He took the company public in 2021, when it got listed at a 68% premium to the IPO price.
His son Mehul, who has an MBA from the University of Pittsburgh, is the managing director and group CEO.
